items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Tick, Black Benny, Lewis, and myself, and Henry Martin... we come back playing, you know, the blues stuff on the street.

ctx.x: Did you see any changes in the brass bands from the time you got here to the time you left, say, 1919 to 1940?

Well, yeah, from what I can see, Tick, Black Benny, Lewis, and myself, and Henry Martin. Yeah. And some of them did change it while I was here. And after one big parade one day, we come back playing, you know, the blues stuff on the street. They didn't play blues on the street. Henry, and then Rosino decided to play some blues, play them fast, you know. Henry who? Henry Martin, I mean, not Henry Rosino. And we come back playing the blues in an up-tempo, you know, where you could walk right along with us, see. And…

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I had Kid Ora, Bischie, Johnny Dodds, now I took Lewis plays, Baby Dodds on drums.

ctx.x: Who was in the band at the 25s?
Well, I had Kid Ora, Bischie, Johnny Dodds, now I took Lewis plays, Baby Dodds on drums. Then you know piano, huh? Two clarinets, huh?
